title: Quantitative Analysis of Cell and Tissue Shape During Mouse Cranial Neural Tube Closure
author: Kristina A. Borys
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare PBTriton solution
steps.instruction: Mix 100 mL of 10× PBS with 1 mL Triton X‑100 (0.1% v/v) and 899 mL deionized water to make 1 L of 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X‑100 (PBTriton); store at 4 °C for up to one year.

steps.title: Prepare blocking solution
steps.instruction: Combine 100 mL of 10× PBS, 1 mL Triton X‑100 (0.1% v/v), and 100 g BSA (10% w/v) with 899 mL deionized water to make 1 L of 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X‑100 + 10% BSA; store at 4 °C for up to one year (add 0.05% sodium azide if desired).

steps.title: Dissect embryos
steps.instruction: In ice‑cold PBS, dissect mouse embryos (E7.5–E8.75) removing yolk sac and amnion; optionally collect allantois or posterior tissue for genotyping.

steps.title: Fix embryos
steps.instruction: Place embryos in 500 µL of 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS per well of a 24‑well plate; incubate 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Transfer embryos between wells
steps.instruction: Using a plastic transfer pipette, gently squeeze near the mouth, pull just enough liquid to hold the embryo, keep constant pressure, and move the embryo to the next well; if embryos do not enter the liquid, gently shake or stir the submerged pipette tip.

steps.title: Wash embryos (first series)
steps.instruction: Wash embryos three times with 1 mL PBTriton per wash, 30 min each at room temperature on an orbital shaker (~60 rpm).

steps.title: Block embryos
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL blocking solution to each well and incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare 500 µL blocking solution containing rabbit anti‑N‑cadherin at 1:500 dilution; incubate embryos 1–2 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Wash embryos (second series)
steps.instruction: Wash embryos three times with 1 mL PBTriton per wash, 30 min each at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Secondary antibody & phalloidin incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare 500 µL blocking solution containing donkey anti‑rabbit AlexaFluor 488 (1:500) and AlexaFluor 546‑phalloidin (1:1000); incubate embryos 1–2 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C, protecting from light with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Wash embryos (third series)
steps.instruction: Wash embryos three times with 1 mL PBTriton per wash, 30 min each at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Store stained embryos
steps.instruction: Keep embryos in PBTriton at 4 °C, covered with aluminum foil, for up to two weeks (prefer imaging earlier).

steps.title: Prepare agarose imaging dish
steps.instruction: Melt low‑melt agarose to 2 % (w/v) in PBS, pour into a 35 mm plastic or glass Petri dish until half full, allow to cool and solidify; keep dish damp and refrigerated for reuse.

steps.title: Warm microscope and accessories
steps.instruction: Turn on brightfield microscope, camera, and gooseneck lamps; allow them to warm up before imaging.

steps.title: Add liquid to imaging dish
steps.instruction: Fill the agarose pad with enough PBTriton to fully cover the embryos.

steps.title: Transfer embryo to imaging dish
steps.instruction: Using a transfer pipette, gently suction the embryo with minimal liquid, keep pressure while moving the pipette tip below the liquid surface in the agarose dish, and release the embryo.

steps.title: Capture brightfield images
steps.instruction: With forceps, position the embryo and acquire three orientations: (1) dorsal view (embryo ventral side down), (2) ventral view (embryo dorsal side down), (3) side view (left or right). Use ~40× total magnification (≈1.7 µm/pixel at 1 388 × 1 040 pixels) and keep magnification constant; record a scale bar image if the microscope does not embed scale.

steps.title: Dispose or store agarose dish
steps.instruction: After imaging, either refrigerate the agarose dish for later use or discard it.

steps.title: Assemble Attofluor imaging chamber
steps.instruction: Place a 25 mm round coverslip in the bottom piece of the aluminum Attofluor chamber, dust both sides, screw the top piece on finger‑tight.

steps.title: Apply vacuum grease
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL syringe filled with Molykote grease and a 200 µL pipette tip, place small dabs or lines of grease on the two parallel edges of a small cover‑glass piece.

steps.title: Position cover‑glass piece
steps.instruction: Place the greased cover‑glass piece at an angle onto the bottom coverslip, then gently press the edges to create a seal.

steps.title: Add buffer to chamber
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL PBTriton to the Attofluor chamber; check for leaks by placing the chamber on a Kimwipe.

steps.title: Mount embryo for confocal
steps.instruction: Place the embryo dorsal side down on the bottom coverslip, slide it under the cover‑glass piece, and gently push with forceps to lightly sandwich it without over‑compression (avoid stretching, bulging, or flattening).

steps.title: Protect mounted sample from light
steps.instruction: Cover the chamber with aluminum foil for the remainder of the procedure.

steps.title: Set confocal acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Mount the chamber on a confocal microscope; use a 40× oil immersion objective, 1 024 × 1 024 pixel frame, 0.35 µm/pixel, bi‑directional scan, acquire all channels at each z‑plane before moving to the next; set laser power and detector gain based on 2–3 test embryos to avoid oversaturation and keep settings constant for the entire litter.

steps.title: Acquire z‑stack and optional tiles
steps.instruction: Collect a z‑stack covering the full depth of the cranial neural plate centered on the lateral midbrain; optionally acquire tiled images with ~10 % overlap (or a separate midline stack if tiling is unavailable).

steps.title: Generate projections and save data
steps.instruction: Create a maximum‑intensity projection of each z‑stack; save both the original z‑stack files and the projections for future reuse.

steps.title: Define regions of interest
steps.instruction: For each embryo, select a 100 µm × 100 µm ROI in the left lateral neural fold (or paired left/right) and a 100 µm × 100 µm ROI at the midline for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Reuse mounting chamber
steps.instruction: After imaging, lift the cover‑glass piece with forceps, retrieve the embryo, and mount a new embryo using the same steps; replace the grease when adhesion diminishes (typically after 2–3 embryos).
